target_customer: Electricity network operators and utilities, such as distribution system operators, running grid planning and connections workflows
problem: Grid planning is done in scattered spreadsheets, static reports and separate network models. Squid keeps one versioned, governed network model with scenarios and assumptions, plus AI assisted studies that engineers review.
business_model: B2B software for utilities; design partner stage, pricing not found
product_category: Model repository and AI assisted planning software for power systems

founders.name: Conor Jones
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. Education not listed.

founders.name: George Kolokotronis
previous_startups: Repeat Energy (described on YC page as repeat energy and CleanTech founder, outcome not stated)

competitors.name: ThinkLabs AI
competitors.what: Physics informed AI agent for grid conditions and distribution system state estimation, launched March 2025
competitors.funding_then: pulse2 reports a $5M raise; later a $28M Series A per a separate listing

competitors.name: IFS Copperleaf
competitors.what: Integrated planning solution for electric utilities extending its asset investment planning platform, launched October 2025
competitors.traction_then: established vendor, no figures in source

competitors.name: envelio Strategic Grid Planner
competitors.what: Loadflow based multi-year distribution planning tool evaluating many planning alternatives

technical_complexity.rationale: Must import models from several incumbent engineering formats (PowerFactory, PSS/E, IPSA, CYME, ETAP) and keep power system results trustworthy; the team has years of grid software experience.

defensibility.rationale: Once a utility keeps its approved baseline model and history in the repository, switching is costly, but incumbents with existing planning suites can add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Schneider launched a digital grid platform with AI model tuning in late 2025 and IFS Copperleaf launched integrated planning in October 2025; no acquisition of Squid reported.

market_need_then: Electrification is increasing connection requests and planning load on operators; the founders cite years of seeing planning stuck in spreadsheets, and National Grid DSO piloted a Squid built tool.

branding.domain_note: Uses squid.energy, a keyword top level domain rather than squid.com

identity.logo: SVG logo file on site; design not described by sources
identity.mascot_or_character: Squid emoji used in the YC profile name and job posts
identity.voice_and_tone: Short declarative headlines such as The grid has a repo now, confident and technical for regulated utilities

branding.brand_signature: The squid emoji and the line The grid has a repo now

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable animal name with an emoji tie in and a witty tagline, but no press or community about the brand and the name is shared with the unrelated Squid proxy software.

outcome_analysis: Squid is a Winter 2026 London company founded by an ex-National Grid and Octopus Energy team, with a live pilot at National Grid DSO and certifications claimed, so no outcome yet. The founders have clear domain access, but large vendors such as Schneider and IFS Copperleaf were shipping AI planning tools in 2025, and the amount raised is unknown.
notes: The company site lists backers Y Combinator, 20VC, Leap Forward Ventures and 33East but gives no amount, date or stage, so the round is stage other with null amount and date. Aggregators (StartupHub, VCBacked, NeuronFeed) say $500K total, a seed or pre-seed in January 2026; unverified and not recorded as an amount. Founding year conflicts: StartupHub says 2023, YC page says 2026. Site says live with National Grid DSO and cites ISO 27001 and SOC 2, company claims. The company site does not name founders; names come from the YC page. Outcome search found no news of acquisition or shutdown.
